summary: Ernst Johann Eitel worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Georgii-Gymnasium Esslingen, Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren, and the University of Tübingen, later serving as professor/lektor in German language and literature at the University of Adelaide (circa 1897–1908).

Ernst Kuhn was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, and Heidelberg, under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Halle, Leipzig, Heidelberg, and Munich (1877–1917).

Ernst Leumann specialized in Indology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Zurich, Geneva, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, Leipzig, and Strasbourg. He worked on the Sanskrit-English Dictionary at Oxford and held professorships at Frauenfeld, Strasbourg, and Freiburg.

Ernst Moritz Arndt worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Greifswald (circa 1791–1793) and the University of Jena (circa 1793–1794), and later held posts at the University of Greifswald and the University of Bonn.

Ernst Osiander was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren and at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as a Repetent at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren and at Tübinger Stift.

Ernst Schwarz was a linguist who studied at the German University of Prague and the Prüfungs-kommission für das Lehramt an Mittelschulen in Prag. He held a post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from circa 1948 to 1963.

Ernst Steinkellner specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner, later serving as director at the University of Vienna and at the Austrian Academy of Sciences' Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Ernst Trumpp worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Tübinger Stift under Rudolf von Roth, held a post at East India House, and served as Privatdozent at Tübingen and professor at the University of Munich (circa 1874–1885).

Ernst Waldschmidt specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Kiel and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders, August Hermann Francke, Albert Grünwedel, Paul Deussen, and Emil Sieg, and held the Indology chair at Göttingen (1936–1965).

Ernst Windisch worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig under Georg Curtius, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, Friedrich Zarncke, and Hermann Brockhaus, later holding chairs at Heidelberg and Strasbourg, and teaching at Leipzig from 1869.
Ernst Zinn was a linguist who held academic posts at the University of Hamburg (circa 1946–1951), Saarland University (1951–1956), and the University of Tübingen (circa 1951–1978).

Erwin Rousselle studied at Munich, Heidelberg, Freiburg, Berlin, and Darmstadt, training under F. E. A. Krause, Max Walleser, and Alexander von Staël-Holstein. He taught at Peking, Tsinghua, and Frankfurt universities, and directed the Sino-Indian Institute and China-Institut Frankfurt.
Esben Andreasen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies who studied at the University of Copenhagen and served as a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.

Eshin Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Hanazono University, under Zenkei Shibayama, at Pendle Hill Quaker Center, and at Kyoto University. He taught at Carleton College and served as director at Hanazono University.
Esho Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as director of the Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).

Esho Mikogami was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University from circa 1973 to 2003 and was president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997.

Esho Sasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who served as an assistant professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and as a professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).
Esho Yamaguchi worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and held posts at Ritsumeikan University and as a professor at Osaka University from circa 1970 to 1982.
Eshun Otsuka is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was a research student (研究生) at Taisho University (attested 2013).

Ester Bianchi works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD studying under Jean-Noël Robert and Alfredo Cadonna at Ca' Foscari and EPHE, and has held posts at Venice, Florence, and the University of Perugia.
